description: SENCORS is the network of continuously operating GNSS reference stations of Senegal, presented on the national geodesy portal. The portal shows the network status (operating normally at the last update on 22 July 2026) and links a cartographic portal of Senegalese geodesy, a Leica portal for the CORS stations, a RINEX portal for downloading files and reporting incidents, and a Circe web service for coordinate transformation. A news post explains that the main control centre suffered disk failures that damaged databases and put the network out of service, that it was migrated to new infrastructure with a secondary control centre, that real-time network RTK corrections are served by NTRIP from caster.geodesie.sn on port 2101, that users must recreate their accounts, and that five new stations from a JICA project (DKR1, FATI, MBOU, NDAN, TIVA) are integrated. Access is through a user account; the cost and terms are not stated on the pages read. Caveats: the network had a recent outage, the station list is not on the home page, and the site is in French. Coverage is Senegal. It supports studies of positioning infrastructure resilience and space weather effects on GNSS in West Africa; related records are BF-CORS of Burkina Faso and the ANCFCC permanent GNSS network of Morocco.
